title: High-precision ab initio calculations of nuclear binding energies: Tin isotopes from dripline to dripline
authors: Urban Vernik, Pepijn Demol, Thomas Duguet, Alexander Tichai
abstract: The location of the neutron drip line in tin isotopes has important consequences for our fundamental understanding of nuclear structure and nuclear forces as well as for astrophysical nucleosynthesis. Performing high-precision ab initio calculations of even-even tin isotopes from $N=50$ to $N=126$ based on chiral two- and three-nucleon interactions, the predicted drip-line location is found to be highly sensitive to the employed nuclear interactions and to exhibit tension with recent energy-density-functional predictions. On the neutron-deficient side, results are consistent with extrapolated two-neutron separation energies constrained by recent Penning-trap mass measurements.
summary: This work applies high-precision ab initio calculations using Bogoliubov Coupled-Cluster theory to determine the binding energies of tin isotopes near the neutron drip line. By incorporating triples correlations, the authors significantly improve theoretical accuracy and map out how nuclear structure predictions conflict with existing Energy Density Functional models regarding exotic nuclei.
main_problem: To perform high-precision ab initio calculations of nuclear binding energies for tin isotopes across the neutron drip line.
main_result: The predicted location of the neutron drip line is highly sensitive to the employed nuclear interactions and shows tension with recent Energy Density Functional predictions. The inclusion of triples corrections significantly improves accuracy by reducing uncertainty from tens of MeV to below 3 MeV in key isotopes.
method: Bogoliubov Coupled-Cluster (BCC) theory, specifically utilizing the BCCSD[T] approximation to account for leading three-body correlations beyond standard CCSD calculations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on even-even Tin (Sn) isotopes ($Z=50$) ranging from $N=50$ up to $N=126$. Calculations are based on realistic chiral Effective Field Theory ($\chi$EFT) two- and three-nucleon interactions.
key_observables: Binding energies ($E_0$), two-neutron separation energies ($S_{2n}$), and the predicted location of the neutron drip line.
important_parameters: The calculations use a spherical harmonic oscillator basis ($\hbar\omega = 12$ MeV) and are sensitive to the specific $\chi$EFT Hamiltonian employed (e.g., $1.8/2.0 (	ext{EM})$ vs. $\Delta-	ext{N}2	ext{LOGO}$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve truncating the cluster expansion at BCCSD[T] and using a specific basis set, leading to residual uncertainties from missing higher-body correlations ($T_{k\ge 4}$) and basis incompleteness.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares ground-state energies calculated with BCCSD vs. BCCSD[T] against experimental values for Sn isotopes; Figure 2 and 3 show $S_{2n}$ around the $N=50$ shell closure and beyond $N=82$, respectively.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework of BCC theory, progresses from BCCSD to the improved BCCSD[T] approximation by solving for triples correlations non-iteratively, applies this method to calculate binding energies across the Sn isotopic chain, and discusses the implications for nuclear structure models like EDFs.
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear physics, the use of advanced many-body quantum field theory techniques (like coupled-cluster expansions) to solve complex Hamiltonians shares conceptual overlap with methods used in strongly correlated electron systems or open quantum system dynamics.
